address: Haarlemmerweg 325, Amsterdam-West (Westergasfabriek district): Q-Park Westergasfabriek, a curved multi-storey car park with brick-fronted shops on its ground floor and three decks screened by pale translucent louvres, and a concrete south front with the car-park entrance
notes: Haarlemmerweg 325 (BAG pand 0363100012110408, built 1913 per BAG; the building is the Q-Park Westergasfabriek multi-storey car park with shops, 107 3DBAG wall surfaces, roof max 19.1 m): a roughly 50 m by 40 m car-park block on the Haarlemmerweg. Photographed: the north front (w01-359 2023: a brick plinth with shopfronts and a LEEN BAKKER and SANIDIRECT fascia, three decks of translucent louvre screens above), the west front (w02-269: same, with badkamers shopfronts), the south front (w04-179: brick corner with the Leen Bakker shop) and the south entrance (w05-168: concrete decks and the car-park entrance under a dark canopy with the Q PARK WESTERGASFABRIEK sign). w03-78 (east) has no usable view.

walls[0] = panel 64 (N, 51 m, eaves 15.2; surfaces 70, 100, 101): 4 storeys x 13 bays of wide ribbon windows over a glazed shopfront ground (14.1k triangles at the default pitch). walls[1] = panel 11 (W, 50 m; surface 13) and walls[2] = panel 10 (S, 38 m; surface 11): the same. walls[3] = panel 50 (S entrance, 15 m, eaves 15.2; surface 54): concrete render, four open ribbon decks over a blank ground, an entrance with a canopy carrying the Q PARK WESTERGASFABRIEK sign. Simplified: the louvre screens are ribbon windows in a pale frame colour, the brick plinth is the wall colour under the glazed ground, the curved corners are the 3DBAG facets. Not drawn: the tenant signs (LEEN BAKKER, SANIDIRECT; shop tenants change), the east front and the inner deck ramps.

Refit 2026-10-25 (issue #59): the three parking decks of walls[0-2] are pale translucent louvre screens (w01-359L, w02-269L, w04-179), not ribbon windows: cladding louvres #c4c8c8 at 0.2 m over a dark ground #4a4c4e from 0.27 to 0.95 of the eaves, the decks behind blank, on a purple-brown brick base #7a6052 (between the shaded #57453e and the sunlit #8b7063) with shop windows 0.55 x 0.62 (the photos show a mostly brick ground with shopfronts, not a glass plinth). Kit fix in the same change: louvre slats are drawn in the sheet colour (they were in the dark line slot, so a louvre screen rendered as one dark sheet). walls[3] (w05-168) is open concrete decks: wall #8e9294, the deck voids as continuous low ribbons 0.97 x 0.4 over a 0.42 parapet. Gate misreads, allowed as inferred: on the louvre fronts the photo labels the translucent screen as glazing (0.2-0.65) and the model wall as the dark louvre ground (family paint), so wall family, glazing and columns compare a screen with a wall; walls[3] photo wall #313b44 is the concrete in blue shade under the decks.
